To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N170 reflects structural encoding, and the ‘N400’ and ‘P400’ are likely to reflect subsequent processes involved in the recognition of familiar faces.
the N170 is sensitive to the processing of facial identity, and that the N400f and P600f reflect the identification of familiar faces.
the N170 reflects pre-categorical structural processing of faces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrophysiological investigation of face processing.
the question of how the brain processes visual information.
face perception, face recognition, and the neural basis of face perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the face-specific N170 is a reliable and sensitive indicator of structural encoding processes, and that the ‘N400’ and ‘P400’ are reliable and sensitive indicators of the subsequent processes of familiarity and recognition.
the N170 is a face-sensitive, early ERP component that reflects the structural encoding of faces.
the P600f is a reliable ERP component, which is not affected by the repetition of a familiar face and is still present, when attention is diverted away from the pictural stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N170 is a pre-categorical, structural encoding effect that can be disrupted by prosopagnosia, while the ‘N400’ and ‘P400’ effects reflect subsequent stages in face recognition.
the ERP approach is an excellent tool to investigate the cognitive processes involved in face perception.

the N170 is the first sign of face processing in the brain, the N400 is the sign of the face being identified, the P600 is the sign that the face is being recognized and that the N170, N400 and P600 are all affected when the brain has a problem in processing the face, as is the case in the prosopagnosia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can identify people by their faces.
the N170 is the first ERP component that can be reliably used in clinical settings to assess the integrity of structural encoding of faces.
the N170 reflects pre-categorical structural face encoding, and the N400f/P600f reflect subsequent processes involved in the face identification process.
